advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_crits` call `registry.normalize_criteria` (with the JSON fallback only when rebar is unimportable) instead of re-implementing the membership test against ROUTING.
evidence: _crits line 210: `canonical = label if label in ROUTING else SYNONYMS.get(label, label)`
registry.normalize_criteria (registry.py:219-222): `known = set(effective_criteria(repo_root))` then `canonical = label if label in known else CRITERIA_SYNONYMS.get(label, label)`

overlay.py:452 `ids.difference_update(disabled_builtins(...))` — effective_criteria drops disabled builtins; overlay.py:459-460 keeps their routing entry resolvable, so effective_routing keys ⊋ effective_criteria
docstring line 27-29 claims both are read 'from the SAME production path the gate uses -- registry.effective_routing ... and registry.normalize_criteria'
advisory.finding: `_crits` re-implements criterion normalization (`canonical = label if label in ROUTING else SYNONYMS.get(label, label)`) instead of calling the production `registry.normalize_criteria`, so it does NOT read synonyms 'through the same production path the gate uses' as the docstring claims. The gate's `normalize_criteria` (registry.py:222) tests membership against `effective_criteria` (which EXCLUDES disabled built-ins, overlay.py:452), while the script tests against `ROUTING` = `effective_routing` keys (which INCLUDE disabled built-ins, kept resolvable per overlay.py:459-460). A synonym whose canonical target is a disabled built-in normalizes differently in the two code paths — reintroducing the drift the change purports to eliminate.
scenarios: A project overlay disables a built-in criterion that is also a synonym target
re-running the generator after routing changes and getting a normalization that does not match the gate
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the inline loop in `_crits` with a call to the production `registry.normalize_criteria(raw, repo_root)` when available, matching its `effective_criteria`-based membership rule; keep the ROUTING-based fallback only for the no-rebar checkout.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Normalize the CRIT argument of `--dump-newly-blocking` (and `--block-impact`) through the same synonym map as `_crits`, or reject/warn when the CRIT resolves to a different canonical label.
evidence: newly_blocking line 292: `if not isinstance(f, dict) or criterion not in _crits(f): continue` — RHS is normalized, LHS `criterion` is the raw CLI arg
main line 368: `for criterion, thr in _parse_block_impact_specs(args.dump_newly_blocking)` — CRIT taken verbatim, no normalize call
posture_of('sec') returns UNROUTED (0.95,False) => ceiling=inf, so even the window would admit everything, yet the criterion string still cannot match
advisory.finding: `--dump-newly-blocking CRIT=THR` passes CRIT to `newly_blocking`/`posture_of` un-normalized, but the finding side (`_crits(f)`) IS normalized through the synonym map. Passing a synonym label (e.g. `sec=0.45`) makes `criterion not in _crits(f)` never match (findings carry the canonical `security`), so the dump is silently EMPTY — indistinguishable from a genuine 'no newly-blocking findings' result.
scenarios: Operator adjudicates a flip by CRIT name and copies a synonym label from an older calibration doc
the empty JSON is read as 'this flip adds no findings' and the flip is waved through
advisory.suggested_fix: Normalize each parsed `criterion` via `SYNONYMS.get(criterion, criterion)` (respecting ROUTING membership) before calling `newly_blocking`/`posture_of`, and print a warning when the normalized form differs from the input.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Emit a visible warning (or fail) when the production-import path is unavailable and a fallback/default is used in `_current_impact_model_version`, `_load_routing`, and `_synonyms`, rather than silently returning a hardcoded value or empty routing.
evidence: `_load_routing` lines 109-124: `except Exception: pass` then JSON fallback that can return `{}` (every criterion becomes UNROUTED) with no diagnostic
docstring lines 77-80 explicitly frames the hardcoded default as the prior failure mode this change removes
advisory.finding: The three production-import helpers (`_current_impact_model_version`, `_load_routing`, `_synonyms`) each catch bare `except Exception` and fall through to hardcoded defaults (`"code-v5"`, `{}`, `{"sec":"security",...}`). A partial/mis-configured environment where the import raises AFTER the model has moved past code-v5 will silently analyse the wrong cohort with an empty/incorrect routing table — reproducing the exact 'hardcoded default silently kept analysing a retired cohort' failure the change says it fixes, and the `"code-v5"` literal itself goes stale on the next model bump.
scenarios: Run in a checkout where rebar imports but sidecar.py has moved to code-v6 while the file-regex path also fails
routing JSON files absent/renamed => `_load_routing` returns {} and every criterion silently reports UNROUTED@0.95
advisory.suggested_fix: Log to stderr which path was taken (imported vs JSON-fallback vs hardcoded default) and treat an empty `_load_routing` result as an error rather than a silent all-UNROUTED table.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a corpus-free test pinning newly_blocking() band inclusion: priority==thr included, priority==cur_thr excluded when currently blocking, and unbounded ceiling when UNROUTED/advisory.
evidence: docs/experiments/calibrate_code_review_thresholds.py:285-296: `cur_thr, cur_blocking, _ = posture_of(criterion)` ... `ceiling = cur_thr if cur_blocking else float("inf")` ... `if not (thr <= pri < ceiling): continue`
search of tests/ for `newly_blocking` returns only src/ and plan_replay hits — no test drives the calibration script's newly_blocking()

Existing test_block_impact_columns_are_computed_from_the_surviving_pools (tests/unit/test_code_review_criteria_routing.py:234) pins the sibling block_impact() corpus-free, establishing this class of function is meant to be tested

Named violating input: for a currently-blocking criterion (cur_thr=0.54, cur_blocking=True) a finding at priority==0.54 must be EXCLUDED (upper bound exclusive) and one at priority==thr must be INCLUDED — neither edge is asserted anywhere
advisory.finding: newly_blocking() — the core new function driving --dump-newly-blocking — is untested. Its priority-band logic (`ceiling = cur_thr if cur_blocking else float('inf')` and `thr <= pri < ceiling`) is non-trivial and analogous to the already-pinned block_impact(), yet no test exercises it. A regression that flipped the band to inclusive-upper or open-lower would not be caught.
scenarios: A refactor or typo changes the band bounds
A future edit reverses the cur_blocking/UNROUTED ceiling logic
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test analogous to test_block_impact_columns_... driving _calibrate_module().newly_blocking(_synthetic_corpus(), 'correctness', 0.52) and asserting the returned set matches the [0.52, cur_thr) band exactly, including the boundary findings.

search of tests/ for `_crits`/`_synonyms` shows no coverage of the calibration script's normalization (only unrelated plan_review _crits helpers)

Named violating input: a finding tagged `criteria: ["sec"]` (with `security` present in ROUTING) must accumulate under `security`, and `["sec", "security"]` must dedup to a single `security` row — neither is asserted
advisory.finding: The label-normalization in _crits() — the CORRECTION-A behavior that is the stated purpose of this change (folding `sec`->`security`, `documentation`->`docs` before accumulation) — is untested at the calibration-script level. While registry.normalize_criteria is covered, the script's own accumulation path (`canonical = label if label in ROUTING else SYNONYMS.get(label, label)`) with dedup is new and unverified.
scenarios: A future edit reorders the `label in ROUTING` vs SYNONYMS lookup, silently reintroducing the bogus separate `sec` row the change exists to eliminate
advisory.suggested_fix: With ROUTING/SYNONYMS module globals set on the loaded calibration module, assert module._crits({'criteria':['sec']}) == ['security'] and module._crits({'criteria':['sec','security']}) == ['security'].
